title: Social Security COLA, Explained Simply
bigPicture: A COLA is the yearly adjustment meant to help Social Security and SSI benefits keep up with rising prices. As of November 2, 2026, the latest COLA is 3.6%.
whatYouNeedToKnow: COLA stands for cost-of-living adjustment. Cost-of-living adjustments keep Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits in step with inflation.
The latest COLA is 3.6% for Social Security benefits and SSI payments.
Social Security benefits increase by 3.6% beginning with the December 2026 benefits, which are payable in January 2027.
Federal SSI payment levels also increase by 3.6% for payments made for January 2027. Because January 1 is a holiday, those SSI payments are made at the end of December.

COLAs are based on the increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). The law compares the third-quarter average to the third-quarter average of the last year a COLA took effect, and rounds to the nearest tenth of a percent.
If there is no increase, or the rounded increase is zero, there is no COLA that year.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming the COLA is the same every year. It depends on the CPI-W and can be zero.
Using an old COLA figure. This guide shows the figure as of November 2, 2026, and a new one is set each year.
Confusing a COLA with a raise based on your work. It is an adjustment for price changes.
actionSteps: Check the Social Security Administration's COLA page for the latest announcement.
Remember that the new amount starts with December 2026 benefits, paid in January 2027.
If you receive SSI, note that the increase is for payments made for January 2027.
